FACT-2.formula: Total spent on blue ties is 200

FACT-3.formula: Red ties cost 50% more than blue ones

RULE-1.formula: If blue tie price is p, red ties cost 1.5 times p

RULE-2.formula: If red price is 1.5 times blue price and blue price matches, then red tie price is 60
RULE-2.verify_reason: hardcodes RedTiePrice to 60, ignoring p, so not a general encoding of the relation

RULE-3.formula: If total blue expenditure equals red price times a count, then that count of red ties can be bought
RULE-3.verify_reason: cross-relates blue total cost, red price, and count in a way not justified by problem

RULE-4.formula: If red tie price is r and count q is bought, total red cost is 180
RULE-4.verify_reason: fixes red total cost to 180 irrespective of actual prices/counts; not valid

INF-2.gloss: From INF-1 and RULE-2 by Modus Ponens -> RedTiePrice(n_60)

INF-3.gloss: From FACT-2 and INF-2 by (some arithmetic-based) reasoning -> RedTiesCount(n_3)
INF-3.formula: Budget of 200 at price 60 yields 3 red ties

INF-4.gloss: From INF-3 and INF-2 by Rule-4 -> RedTiesTotalCost(n_180)
